newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen $1 higher, Brent up about 10 cts.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen $1 higher, Brent up about 10 cts.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were expected to open higher on Friday, firming on overnight gains in Singapore, while Brent was also expected to open firmer.

July gas oil is seen opening $1 higher from its closing price of $162.50 a tonne while Brent should at least match a 12 cents gain in Singapore and move 10 to 15 cents higher from its settlement price of $17.44.
With the U.S. market having held up well after London's close, brokers said $164 was an achievable near-term target for July gas oil and if that level was broken the market could move even higher.
"I'm feeling more friendly towards the market," one dealer said. "There didn't seem to be too much selling pressure in the U.S. last night whereas the previous two nights it has come tumbling down."
And concerns that administrative problems might delay the second six month stint of the U.N./Iraq oil-for-food deal buoyed both gas oil and Brent prices, brokers said.

The United Nations on Thursday said a team of its weapons inspectors had twice been blocked from entering a total of three suspected military sites since Tuesday, adding to worries that political posturing by Iraq over the distribution of food might delay the deal.

Brent prices looked likely to be pushed higher by a prompt gain on the expiry of the front-month options contract in the U.S. during London hours, and could reach $19 or even $19.50. But brokers were expecting prices to retreat from those levels after the expiry of the contract.

Details of the July Brent loading programme were unlikely to have an impact on the market as only a small increase in cargoes was reported. And a small fall in Norway's crude cargoes in July would cancel out the increase in Brent supply. The first of Norway's July loading programmes showed the Gullfaks system loading 21 standard cargoes, three down from June.
